title: Real Time Monitoring of Intracellular Bile Acid Dynamics Using a Genetically Encoded FRET-based Bile Acid Sensor
protocol: Harvest cells from an 80% confluent 25 cm2 flask.
Dilute cells in complete culture medium suitable for the specific cell line.
Plate cells at the desired density into a sterile 8 well chambered cover glass.
Add complete culture medium to a final volume of 400 μl per well.
Allow cells to attach for 24 hours.
Prepare the transfection mix in a sterile tube by adding 0.5 µg of NucleoBAS or CytoBAS DNA to 100 µl of culture medium (serum/antibiotic free).
Vortex the mixture well.
Add a transfection reagent and mix by vortexing.
Incubate the DNA/transfection reagent mix for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Add the transfection mixture in droplets to the cells.
Gently shake the well plate by hand to mix.
Add 100 µl of the mixture for each well of approximately 9.6 cm2 area.
Harvest cells from an 80% confluent 25 cm2 flask.
Dilute pellet in complete culture medium suitable for the specific cell line (10% Fetal Bovine Serum, 1% L-glutamine, 1% pen/strep for U2OS and Huh7 cells) to a concentration of 150,000 cells per ml.
Add around 300,000 cells per well in a 6-well culture plate (2 ml end volume).
Allow cells to attach for 24 hr.
Prepare the transfection mix in a sterile tube by adding 0.5 µg of CytoBAS or NucleoBAS DNA to 100 µl of culture medium (serum/antibiotic free).
Vortex well.
Add 2.5 µl of 1 mg/ml polyethylenimine (PEI) and mix by vortexing.
Incubate the DNA/PEI mix for 15 min at RT.
Add 100 µl of the transfection mixture in droplets to the cells and mix by gently shaking the well plate by hand.
Grow cells O/N at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Trypsinize cells according to manufacturer's protocol.
Incubate cells at 37 °C with 1.5 ml prewarmed trypsin per 25 cm² cell culture.
Spin cells down at 250 x g at RT for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 13 ml of complete culture medium.
Divide cells over various 10 cm diameter culture dishes: use 0.5 ml (low density), 1.5 ml (medium density), and 4.5 ml (high density).
Add culture medium to a final volume of 10 ml for U2OS cells, use 800 µg/ml G418 for plasmids with the neomycin resistance cassette such as the CytoBAS and NucleoBAS constructs.
Refresh the culture medium with appropriate antibiotic (G418) every 72 hr until untransfected cells are dead.
Examine the culture plate under the microscope with a 20X objective for positive colonies.
Mark positive colonies that lie isolated from other colonies with a pen on the exterior bottom of the culture dish.
Wash the plate twice with Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS).
Aspirate the PBS from the plate.
Take around 15 sterile cloning cylinders and dip them into sterile silicone.
Apply the cloning cylinders around selected colonies, pressing lightly against the petri-dish to ensure no more than one colony is included in each ring.
Pipette 20 µl of pre-warmed trypsin (1x, 0.25%) into each cloning cylinder.
Incubate at 37 °C until most cells have rounded up, observing under a microscope.
Add 150 µl of culture medium with serum and the appropriate antibiotic to each cloning cylinder.
Pipette up and down several times to resuspend the cells.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 96-well plate.
Refresh the medium after 4-24 hours.
Allow the cells to grow confluent in the next few days at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for U2OS and Huh7 cells.
Refresh the medium with antibiotic every 3 or 4 days.
When the cells have grown confluent, transfer them to a larger well plate.
Repeat this step until the culture is large enough for experiments.
Cryopreserve some vials for backup using cryopreservation medium consisting of 20% FBS and 20% DMSO in media (DMEM) without supplements.
Harvest cells from an 80% confluent 25 cm² flask.
Dilute cells in complete culture medium suitable for the specific cell line.
Add around 200,000 cells per well in a 6-well culture plate.
Incubate cells with culture medium to a final volume of 2 ml per well.
Allow cells to attach for 24 hours.

Perform viral transductions by incubating cells for 4-6 hours with 500 μl CytoBAS lentivirus containing medium filled up to a total amount of 1 ml with complete culture medium containing 10 µg/ml DEAE-dextran.
Include a well with untransduced control cells.
Remove the medium after transduction.
Add 2 ml of complete culture medium containing hygromycin (500 μg/ml).
Refresh medium with hygromycin antibiotic every 3 days.
Split the cells when they reach 80% confluence.
Continue growing cells until all negative control cells are dead, which takes about 1-2 weeks for most cell lines.
Use cells for experiments 1-3 days after viral transduction.
Harvest cells from a confluent 160 cm² flask.
Dilute cells in Leibovitz culture medium (L-15 medium) with <5% serum to a concentration of maximum 5 x 10⁶ cells per ml.
Fill FACS tubes with 1 ml of collection medium (L-15 medium + 1.5% pen/strep, 1% L-glut and 20% serum).
Sort cells for citrine (520-580 nm) or cerulean (450-520 nm), excited with 405 laser.
After sorting approximately 500,000 cells, spin down cells (5 min, 250 x g).
Resuspend the sorted cells in 5 ml of normal complete culture medium (10% FBS, 250 µg/ml Hygromycin for U2OS and Huh7 CytoBAS cells) and plate them in a T25 culture flask.
Grow cells under desired conditions (37 °C, 5% CO₂ for U2OS and Huh7 cells).
Plate cells stably or transiently expressing the sensor into a sterile 8 well coverslip bottomed chamber slide.
Grow cells in complete culture medium until confluency is around 60-70% on the day of the experiment.
Wash adherent cells once with 200 µl of 1x PBS or Leibovitz's L-15 culture medium.
Aspirate and replace with 300 µl of Leibovitz's L-15 culture medium to maintain a constant pH without CO2 control.
Dilute compounds for the confocal imaging experiment in L-15 culture medium, preparing solutions 3-5x concentrated.
Start the imaging software on a confocal microscope with a 37 °C incubation chamber and turn on the violet 405 nm laser.
Place a drop of immersion oil onto the objective and position the 8-chamber slide on top.
Use a 63X oil objective for single cell FRET imaging.
Set the acquisition mode to xyt (time-lapse imaging of single focal plane).
Acquire images at 20 second intervals.
Set spectral range for emission detection: Cerulean, 450-520 nm; Citrine, 520-580 nm.
Focus on the single cell layer using transillumination light.
Adjust z-position more precisely.
Adjust gain and offset for each channel to distinguish signal from background while remaining well below saturation for all pixels in cells of interest.
Draw circles to define the region of interest (ROI).
Select cells that show similar fluorescence intensity.
Avoid cells that obviously differ from the average cell in size and shape.
Expose the cells to light for a time as short as possible to minimize photobleaching of the sensor.
Start measurements with the confocal microscope.
Wait until the cerulean and citrine fluorescence is stable.
Add 50-100 µl of bile acids or other compounds at chosen time points.
Mix fluids well within 10 seconds without shaking or pipetting up and down.
Avoid touching the edge of the 8-well chamber with the pipette tip.
Add liquid slowly to prevent cells from losing focus.
Do not add new compounds before reaching the plateau phase, which takes about 200 seconds.
End each experiment by adding 100 µl of GW4064 at a concentration of 5-10 µM.
Wait until sensor fluorescence is stable after adding GW4064.
Save the experiment and export data as an .AVI file.
Draw regions of interest (ROIs) covering specific cells with the oval selection tool.
Draw one circle in an area outside cells or inside a cell that does not express the sensor to determine the background signal.
Select one cell.
Click on Plugins > Ratio Profiler.
Observe the RAW window for changes in intensity of citrine and cerulean.
Analyze the Ratio window for information about the ratio citrine/cerulean, which increases with an increase in FRET.
Review the Ratio_Profile window for actual numbers of fluorescence intensity measured in both channels.
Copy data from the Ratio_Profile window in the spreadsheet.
Do the same for all other cells and background ROI.
Dilute all compounds for the FACS experiment in sterile FACS uptake buffer.
Harvest cells from an 80% confluent T-160 cm2 cell culture flask using 5 mM EDTA in PBS.
Centrifuge cells at 250 x g for 5 min.
Wash cell pellet 2x in 5 ml FACS uptake buffer at RT.
Count cells using the coulter counter or a counting chamber.
Dilute pellet in FACS uptake buffer to a concentration of 1 x 106 cells/ml.
Pipette up and down to create a homogeneous suspension of single cells.
If cells are difficult to disaggregate, put the samples through a cell strainer before sorting to minimize nozzle clogs.
Pipet 200 µl cells per FACS tube and protect them from light.
Add the desired concentration of the compound (e.g., bile acids, synthetic FXR ligands, transporter inhibitors).
Vortex.
Incubate for 20-30 min at RT while shaking (in the dark).
Meanwhile, start the FACS (the lasers need time to warm up).
Load around 100,000-200,000 NucleoBAS or CytoBAS transfected cells to determine the gates.
Adjust the FSC and SSC voltages to plot the cells in the center of the plot.
Using the violet laser, adjust the cerulean (450/40 nm) voltage value and citrine (525/20 nm) voltage and ensure that all NucleoBAS or CytoBAS positive cells are plotted within the scatter plot.
Set the correct gates (Gate P1 up to Gate P4).
Use gate P1 to exclude dead cells, usually displayed in the lower left corner by selecting the main population in the middle of the SSC-A/FSC-A plot.
Use gate P2 in the FSC-H/FSC-A window to remove duplets from analysis. Single cells are presented in a more diagonal line than doublets.
Gate P3 in the citrine (525/20 nm)/cerulean (450/40 nm) window to select for NucleoBAS/CytoBAS positive cells.
Gated citrine and cerulean high cells, a population displayed diagonally in the upper right corner of the plot.
Draw gate P4 at the top left of the population as close as possible.
Ensure no more than 5% of the cells fall within this gate.
Load untransfected cells to determine auto-fluorescence.
Vortex the samples before placing the tubes in the FACS.
Measure at least 10,000 cells in gate P3 for each sample.
